edge.subject: Liquid electrolytes confined in GO nanochannel membranes
edge.object: Maximum ionic Seebeck coefficient of −0.400 ± 0.038 mV K−1
edge.conditions: KCl concentration 0.1 mM; temperature difference 24 K; electrode thermogalvanic contribution isolated; reported as a maximum.
edge.quote: In this study, we experimentally and numerically investigate the thermoelectric response of both monovalent and multivalent liquid electrolytes in graphene oxide (GO) nanochannel membranes, using KCl as a representative system, to elucidate the governing mechanisms.
context_quotes: By isolating the thermogalvanic contribution of the electrodes, the results reveal that the observed ionic Seebeck coefficient of GO nanochannels is governed by a competition between Soret-type ion thermodiffusion and ion diffusion driven by temperature-dependent ion electrophoretic mobility (TDIEM).

The ionic Seebeck coefficient increases with decreasing electrolyte concentration and increasing temperature difference, accompanied by enhanced surface charge density, and reaches a maximum value of -0.400 +/- 0.038 mV/K at a KCl concentration of 0.1 mM under a temperature difference of 24 K.

edge.subject: Liquid-flow thermocell
edge.object: Ionic thermopower: -21.5 mV K-1; 13 times larger than pristine liquid-state thermocells
edge.quote: Here, we demonstrate a liquid-flow thermocell (LFTC) with giant thermoelectric performance by inducing hybrid entropy increasing.
